HCBCOGN312.name: Psycholinguistics
HCBCOGN312.contribution: examines language processing and its cognitive and neural bases
HCBCOGN312.topics: Psycholinguistics is the study of the neurobiological and psychological factors that enable us to acquire, use, and understand language. Modern research draws on cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and computer science to investigate how language is processed. The course focuses primarily, though not exclusively, on the neuroscience of language. Students examine theoretical and experimental issues in speech production and comprehension, language impairments, the relationship between thought and language, and the evolution and acquisition of language. They also gain hands-on experience with experimental approaches to the study of language and develop an understanding of human linguistic capacity as a subject of multidisciplinary research. Topics covered: What is language? Evolutionary aspects of language and animal communication; language and thought; aphasia; language acquisition; bilingualism; speech comprehension; semantics; reading and dyslexia; speech production.

analysis: The broad plan combines biological and cognitive psychology, lifespan development, health and social psychology with qualitative methods, quantitative methods and evidence synthesis. Psychology of Organizations & Leadership adds genuine work psychology through motivation, team dynamics and organizational behavior. The clinical and lifespan plan adds a coherent health-science cluster in epidemiology, pharmacology and disease mechanisms, linked to psychopathology, diagnosis, psychotherapy and psychological development. The cognition plan instead adds cell biology, functional anatomy, biological laboratory methods and computational data work to the sustained perception, language and higher cognition sequence. Psycholinguistics provides substantive acquisition and processing evidence on the strength of its course description. Programming complements behavioral data methods, while biomedical courses are biological foundations rather than specialist clinical training. A paired OU module requires shared academic substance: general machine learning does not teach psychometrics, and persuasion does not reproduce structured interviewing. The selected diagnostic course overlaps with psychological assessment, with separate OU interviewing and longitudinal research left visible. No route confers the comparator degree or professional qualification. UCR independent research is outside the planned 180 EC.
